I know it's a long question but I just want to know if people get that amazing feeling when you find music you love.
How did you discover your favorite band/musician? What were your first thoughts, and how did their music make you feel?

First off, how about you?

My favorite is DCFC. At first I did not like most of their music. I started off with Sound of Settling and I Will Possess Your Heart. As I went through Plans, Photo Album, Narrow Stairs, and Translanticism it just seemed to fit my mood at the time. It made me feel somewhat apathetic, while realizing the beauty in life. The rhythm of the music is perfect. The transitioning from song to song in their albums is somewhat melancholy and hypnotizing.

I do not listen to them as much anymore. Mainly a ton of chillstep and acoustic these days. The Tallest Man on Earth is one of the best artists you have never heard of. The Bob Dylan of today living in Ireland haha.

I love Bo Burnham. I remember my friends brother showed me his early youtube videos and I just thought about how funny he was. I also love Watsky, I just went to one of his concerts and it was phenomenal. I had moments of pure ecstasy and it was great. The funny part is I also remember watching his raps fast video and being quite impressed and it all started with that.

The first song was Monkey Gone to Heaven. I remember listening to it on car journeys because it was one of the songs on my father's Mix-Tape. It always struck me as just being a funny song and I didn't listen to the Pixies properly until something like 7 years later when I was stealing CDs from my dad and I came across Wave of Mutilation, Pixies Best of album. Over the next few months I listened to very little else and over time bought all the albums I could find. More than once I cleared out an HMV's stock of Pixies CDs.
Pixies are a timeless band. The music will always sound good.

I was watching a Les Claypool concert dvd and he was using a green bullet mic with SANDMAN written on it. He then explained the meaning behind the mic and I found out about Morphine and Mark Sandman. The music encompasses a range of emotion and you get the impression the songs are biographical and others are just a string of good words over some great music. I listened to the Cure For Pain album and was hooked on the first listen. I would recommend getting a copy of the documentary Cure For Pain The Mark Sandman Story.
